clue.text: Bolted, say, ordinary passable rubbish

parts.note: to bolt food is to wolf or gulp it down
say means for example, abbreviated e.g.
OK means acceptable or passable

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a string of words as merely passable nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Unintelligible jargon is a synonym for rubbish talk or nonsense.

clue.text: Girls engaged in some hosting and serving initially

definitions.text: Girls engaged in some hosting and serving initially

indicators.note: initially tells us to take the opening letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: Young women are employed to host guests and serve them.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: the first letters of its seven words spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Japanese hostesses trained to entertain and serve guests are exactly girls engaged in hosting and serving.

clue.text: Heraldic symbol concerning noble

parts.note: a bar is a horizontal band on a coat of arms
on means about or concerning, as in a talk on history

explanation.surface: A coat-of-arms device relating to an aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-ranking peer in the British nobility holds this title.

clue.text: Member arrives behindhand to pass law

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
someone who arrives behindhand is late, giving 'is late'

explanation.surface: An MP turns up late for a vote that passes a law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests a Member of Parliament, but it is a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: Parliaments make statutes, and to make statutes is to pass law.

clue.text: Last of Highland drink in glen

indicators.note: the final letter of the word Highland is wanted

parts.note: ale is beer, a drink

explanation.surface: A dram drunk at the end of a Highland day in a glen.
explanation.definitionFit: A valley, especially in northern England; a glen is the Scottish word for a valley.

clue.text: Train roaring around second station

indicators.note: around has the rearranged letters surround the next piece
to train something is to direct or shape it, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A noisy train roars past a second railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' and 'station' look like railway words; ROARING rearranged gives GARRION, around S.
explanation.definitionFit: To post troops at a place is to station them there; a body of troops posted is also a station.

clue.text: Harangue over tax

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
a rate is a local tax or levy

explanation.surface: Someone lectures loudly about taxation.
explanation.definitionFit: To harangue is to speak at length in a pompous, declaiming way, i.e. to hold forth.

clue.text: Clean horrible stain on one's evening top

indicators.note: a horrible mess suggests the letters of stain are jumbled

parts.note: one is I, and one's is read as 'one is', giving I plus S

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone must wash an awful mark off their evening top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horrible' rearranges STAIN to SANIT; 'evening top' looks like a garment but is just E.
explanation.definitionFit: To disinfect or make hygienic is a synonym for clean as a verb.

clue.text: Honour always pinned by Queen getting elevated

indicators.note: pinned by means held inside the other piece
in a down clue, elevated means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina
ever means always

explanation.surface: A loyal subject is honoured by the Queen, perhaps with a raised status.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting elevated' turns ER upward to RE, which then holds EVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To respect deeply or venerate someone is to honour them.

clue.text: Partisan guerrilla manoeuvres, deposing left for right

indicators.note: manoeuvres suggests the letters are moved about into a new order
deposing one letter for another means replacing it

explanation.surface: Guerrilla fighters manoeuvre, overthrowing the left in favour of the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deposing left for right' swaps one L in GUERRILLA for R, giving GUERRIRLA, which is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan is a fighter in an unofficial force, a soldier who is not regular.

clue.text: Open pastry dish empty on stove

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after

parts.note: an Aga is a British range cooker found in many country kitchens

indicators.note: empty removes the inside of the word, here its middle letter

parts.note: a pie is a pastry dish

explanation.surface: An open pie sits on the stove with nothing in it.
explanation.walkthrough: An AGA is a heavy British range cooker; emptying PIE leaves PE.
explanation.definitionFit: Wide open, as of a gaping mouth; both mean gaping.

clue.text: Blunt? Sharpen and sculpt edges

parts.note: to hone a blade is to sharpen it

indicators.note: edges are the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A sculptor asks whether a tool is blunt and sharpens it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blunt' and 'Sharpen' look like opposites about a blade; Blunt means frank.
explanation.definitionFit: Blunt speech is frank and candid, which is truthful speaking.

clue.text: Means to save one trapped by large cat

indicators.note: trapped by means held inside the other pieces

parts.note: feline is a cat
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone is cornered by a big cat and needs rescuing.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope thrown to rescue someone, or any rescue measure, is a means of saving them.

clue.text: Run naked with redhead in small wood

indicators.note: in places the red's head inside the other pieces

parts.note: teak is a hardwood
the head of the word red is its first letter, R

explanation.surface: Someone runs naked with a red-haired friend through a little wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redhead' looks like a person but gives only the first letter of red.
explanation.definitionFit: To dash naked through a public place is a synonym for running naked.

clue.text: Run without hindrance in game involving chance

indicators.note: without means outside, so the run goes round the other piece

parts.note: a route is a run, as in a bus or delivery run
a let is a hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: Someone runs freely in a game of chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without hindrance' reads as the idiom for freely, but 'without' means outside. A let in tennis is a hindered serve, replayed.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino wheel where players bet on where a ball lands is a game of chance.

clue.text: Criminal's priors oddly preceding Ecstasy scheme

parts.note: a con is a convict or criminal, so criminal's is CON plus S

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of the word

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A criminal with previous convictions plots something involving the drug Ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'priors' looks like a criminal record; 'oddly' keeps its 1st, 3rd and 5th letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To plot together in secret, as a verb, is to scheme.

clue.text: Feeling thrilled over blokes consumed by sex

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above the following pieces

parts.note: sent means thrilled, enraptured

indicators.note: consumed by means swallowed inside another piece

parts.note: it is slang for sex
blokes are men

explanation.surface: A thrilled feeling about men absorbed by sex.
explanation.walkthrough: IT is an old slang word for sex or sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: An emotion or opinion is a feeling; the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Almost loose pass before England game

indicators.note: almost means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: lax means slack or loose
a cross is a pass of the ball across the field

explanation.surface: A sloppy pass before an England match.
explanation.definitionFit: A team sport played with netted sticks is a game.

clue.text: Watched range, as some say it's for cooking

indicators.note: as some say signals that the words sound like the answer when spoken

parts.note: saw means watched; a span is a range or extent

explanation.surface: Someone watched a kitchen range, as people say it's for cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' looks like a cooker, but means a span; spoken in a non-rhotic accent SAW SPAN sounds like the pan.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-handled cooking pot is something for cooking.

clue.text: Cried terribly putting blonde head on mattress

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above

parts.note: so means very or terribly, as in so sorry

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a bed is a mattress

explanation.surface: Someone wept bitterly with a blonde head on the mattress.
explanation.definitionFit: Wept with convulsive gasps, a synonym of cried.

clue.text: Make attractive rear prominent feature

parts.note: the end is the rear or back
an ear sticks out from the head, a prominent feature

explanation.surface: Someone's prominent backside is their most attractive feature.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone loved or liked is to make them attractive.

clue.text: Soldiers raised balloon creating UFO scare here?

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: OR stands for Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers
to balloon is to swell

explanation.surface: Soldiers sent up a balloon and caused a UFO panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns OR upward to RO. The 1947 New Mexico incident was officially a weather balloon.
explanation.definitionFit: A New Mexico town famous for a 1947 alleged flying-saucer crash, a place of UFO alarm.

clue.text: In club, let her speak — talks nonsense

indicators.note: in says the letters lie within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: At a club, someone says 'let her speak' about a woman talking nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of club through let her to the start of speak.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scots verb meaning chatters idly or babbles, i.e. speaks foolishly.

clue.text: Person of faith indulged, essentially

indicators.note: essentially points to letters at the core of the words faith indulged

explanation.surface: A believer was spoiled, in essence.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across the end of faith and the start of indulged.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the major religion of India is a person of faith.

clue.text: Thrown round?

parts.note: looks like a punch thrown in a boxing round, but describes a round object hurled in athletics

explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a boxing round; it is a noun for a circular object that is thrown.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy circular plate hurled in field athletics is a round thing thrown.

clue.text: Heartless cricketer that is getting runs, he declares

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricketer gets runs and declares the innings closed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'declares' looks like cricket's declaration, but means announces publicly.
explanation.definitionFit: A town official who made public announcements is someone who declares things.

clue.text: Chief of staff welcoming number one

indicators.note: welcoming means taking another piece inside

parts.note: to man a post is to staff it
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A chief of staff greets the top person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chief of staff' reads as a job title; Chief is the definition and staff is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Principal or most important, an adjective sense shared with chief.

clue.text: Consumed tuck in school, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken, so the word sounds like the school's name

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: Snacks are wolfed down at boarding school, so it's said.
explanation.walkthrough: Tuck is British school slang for snacks; 'tuck in' is just the surface, eating at Eton, the English public school.
explanation.definitionFit: Past participle meaning used up or devoured, as food is consumed.

clue.text: Drunk takes in beer, half cut — mixed drink

indicators.note: drunk means the letters stagger into a new order
half cut means the word is cut in half, keeping the first half

explanation.surface: A drunk downs beer, half cut, and moves on to a cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half cut' looks like British slang for tipsy; it keeps BE from beer, mixed with TAKESIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A lager-and-cider mix, often with blackcurrant, is a mixed drink.

clue.text: Changing usual partner is weird

indicators.note: changing tells us the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Swapping one's normal partner is odd behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Beyond the natural, paranormal and therefore uncanny or weird.
